## What it is

An open-top box for drying seeds, with rounded vertical corners and side
walls that lean outward a few degrees going up. The lean means an empty
box's bottom drops down into another one's open top, so a stack of them
takes up a lot less shelf height than the same boxes with straight walls.

## Design notes

`wall_angle` is the lean in degrees from vertical; 8 degrees is enough
lean that, with the default wall and height, one box's bottom actually
sinks a few millimetres into the next one's open top rather than just
resting on its rim. `corner_radius` rounds the four vertical corners for
a cleaner first-layer peel front. Wall thickness sets both the floor and
the side walls, measured perpendicular to the (leaning) wall, not
straight down.

## Don't

- Don't trust that any outward lean nests two boxes: below a certain
  angle (for the defaults, under about 6.7 degrees) the taper doesn't
  accumulate enough width over the box's height to let one box's bottom
  fit inside another's open top at all, and they just rest flush,
  rim on rim, with no stacking benefit. The part refuses to build below
  that angle rather than silently failing to stack, and names the
  angle that fixes it.
- Don't shell this with a plain offset: offsetting a tapered solid fails
  in the kernel. The cavity is built as its own tapered solid, sized a
  wall's thickness smaller all round, and cut from the outer one.
- Don't filter the bed-touching edges out of polish with a bare `> bed`
  comparison: a tapered wall's bottom rim lands a hair off the bed's
  exact Z value from kernel float noise, and without a tolerance polish
  chamfers that rim, which is a first-layer overhang the printer can't
  hold. Keep the 0.01mm tolerance.

## Changelog

- Rebuilt as a hollow, open-top box (it was a solid block with an unused
  `wall` parameter before). Added rounded vertical corners
  (`corner_radius`) and outward-leaning walls (`wall_angle`) so stacked
  boxes nest into each other.
- Checked the nesting against the real geometry (not just eyeballing the
  lean): 5 degrees turned out to give zero sink, boxes only rested rim
  on rim. Raised the default lean to 8 degrees, which sinks about a
  quarter of the box height into the one below, and added a refusal for
  any height/wall/angle combination too shallow to nest at all.
